why: Checks 1 and 2 only assert values that the expect words require: left padding to width, a space as the default fill, and s returned unchanged when long enough. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition needs the regex `^#+\s+<name>\b` to print `missing: none`. The words only require "a section for every function". A valid section headed "## `padLeft(...)`" (in backticks) or "## The padLeft function" would fail. That is a heading-format rule the words don't force, and it is in PASS/FAIL rather than under Advisory. Check 4 also requires the summary to show the exact text `# fail 0` on top of exit 0. That is stricter than "npm test passes", and Node's spec reporter doesn't print that line.
